title: Treat Claude Code as an agent with a feedback loop
summary: Give it a goal, let it inspect and act, then require observable verification.
explanation: Agentic coding is strongest when exploration, implementation, and verification form a closed loop rather than a single answer.
whyItWorks: Tools expose real repository state and tests provide correction signals.
whenNotToUse: When no safe verification exists without human review
example: Implement the parser, run focused tests, inspect the diff, then run the suite.
advancedVariation: Have a fresh reviewer session challenge the result.

title: Write prompts as executable briefs
summary: State outcome, context, constraints, boundaries, and verification.
explanation: A useful prompt narrows the solution space while leaving implementation judgment to the agent.
whyItWorks: The agent can distinguish required behavior from incidental implementation preferences.
whenNotToUse: Tiny obvious edits where the repository already supplies context
example: Add rate limiting to POST /login; preserve the public API; follow existing middleware; add focused tests; do not change dependencies; report commands and residual risks.
advancedVariation: Ask Claude to interview you only for decisions that materially change the solution.

title: Explore before editing
summary: Ask Claude to map relevant code and propose options before a consequential change.
explanation: Planning mode separates reconnaissance and design decisions from mutation.
whyItWorks: Repository evidence can invalidate assumptions before they become code.
whenNotToUse: One-line, well-localized fixes
example: Explain the request path, identify tests and conventions, then give three solutions from simplest to most extensible.
mistakes: Treating the first plan as final
advancedVariation: Use spec → milestone → task list → code, reviewing each boundary.

title: Decompose work until each unit is verifiable
summary: Split large tasks into coherent steps with independent evidence.
explanation: Task size should be limited by reasoning and verification complexity, not merely lines changed.
whyItWorks: Smaller loops reduce hidden assumptions and make recovery cheap.
whenNotToUse: When splitting creates artificial interfaces and coordination overhead
example: First add the data model and tests, then API behavior, then UI, then end-to-end coverage.
advancedVariation: Assign isolated research units to subagents while one session owns integration.

title: Keep context fresh and task-specific
summary: Clear between unrelated tasks and compact deliberately during long work.
explanation: Irrelevant history, failed approaches, and noisy tool output compete with current evidence.
whyItWorks: A clean context improves attention to current constraints.
whenNotToUse: Mid-investigation before recording critical state
example: Create a handoff with goal, decisions, changed files, tests, failures, and next step; then start fresh.
advancedVariation: Use /compact with preservation instructions or rewind to summarize only part of a session.

title: Course-correct early
summary: Stop an incorrect trajectory before it accumulates edits and misleading context.
explanation: Esc interrupts while preserving context; rewind can restore conversation or code state.
whyItWorks: Early correction avoids reasoning built on a false premise.
whenNotToUse: Normal exploration that is gathering useful evidence
example: Stop, state the violated constraint, ask for a revised plan, then proceed only after reviewing it.
mistakes: Waiting until the full change is done
advancedVariation: After two failed corrections, start clean with a prompt incorporating what was learned.

title: Keep CLAUDE.md concise, concrete, and tested
summary: Record stable project-specific instructions, not an encyclopedia.
explanation: Include commands Claude cannot infer, style exceptions, workflow rules, and non-obvious gotchas; prune stale guidance.
whyItWorks: Short, specific instructions are easier to follow and cost less context.
whenNotToUse: Temporary task state
File-by-file codebase descriptions
example: Commands: npm test -- --runInBand. Never edit generated clients; run npm run generate instead.
advancedVariation: Use scoped child files and imports; keep personal overrides local.

title: Prefer direct CLI tools with compact output
summary: Let Claude use established CLIs and request only the slice of output needed.
explanation: Tools such as gh, git, test runners, and cloud CLIs expose structured, reproducible state.
whyItWorks: Compact commands reduce copying and context noise.
whenNotToUse: When credentials or write scope are unclear
example: Use gh run view for the failing job instead of streaming an entire log.
advancedVariation: Poll long jobs with bounded backoff and concise status commands.

title: Provide a trustworthy verification target
summary: Tests, types, lint, runtime probes, and visual checks turn autonomy into a bounded loop.
explanation: Claude can iterate independently only when it can observe whether the result meets the requirement.
whyItWorks: Objective feedback catches errors that self-assessment misses.
whenNotToUse: Never omit human judgment for high-risk behavior
example: Reproduce the bug with a failing test, implement the smallest fix, run focused then broad checks.
mistakes: Tests that only assert implementation details
advancedVariation: Use tmux or browser automation to close loops around interactive systems.

title: Use Git as the durable safety boundary
summary: Review diffs, make intentional commits, and use draft PRs for a reversible review gate.
explanation: Claude checkpoints are useful but do not capture every external or Bash-made change; Git remains the durable record.
whyItWorks: Small commits reveal scope and make rollback and review straightforward.
whenNotToUse: Do not commit secrets or broken intermediate states to shared branches
example: Inspect status and diff, run checks, commit one coherent change, then open a draft PR.
advancedVariation: Use a fresh session to review the diff without authoring bias.

title: Isolate parallel edits with worktrees
summary: Give concurrent sessions separate branches and directories.
explanation: Worktrees prevent filesystem collisions while retaining one repository object store.
whyItWorks: Each agent owns a clear branch and working directory.
whenNotToUse: Tightly coupled edits to the same files
example: One worktree implements; another, with fresh context, reviews or writes tests.
advancedVariation: Limit human coordination load to roughly three or four active streams.

title: Delegate context-heavy, isolated research
summary: Use subagents for independent reads or specialist reviews, not for arbitrary fragmentation.
explanation: A subagent gets a separate context and can return a concise result to the main thread.
whyItWorks: Verbose exploration does not crowd the integration context.
whenNotToUse: Tasks requiring constant shared-state coordination
example: Ask one subagent to map auth flows and another to inspect tests; keep implementation ownership central.
advancedVariation: Specify allowed tools, scope, evidence format, and stopping condition.

title: Package recurring expertise as a skill
summary: A skill combines a concise trigger description with on-demand instructions, references, and scripts.
explanation: Use skills for repeatable domain methods that should load only when relevant.
whyItWorks: Progressive disclosure avoids placing every workflow in global context.
whenNotToUse: One-off prompts
Rules needed in every session
example: A security-review skill defines scope, checks, evidence format, and safe scripts.
advancedVariation: Disable automatic invocation for workflows with side effects.

title: Choose extensions by the missing capability
summary: Use CLAUDE.md for always-on rules, skills for on-demand methods, subagents for isolated work, hooks for deterministic events, and MCP for external capabilities.
explanation: Each extension solves a different context, execution, or integration problem.
whyItWorks: Matching the mechanism prevents context bloat and surprising side effects.
whenNotToUse: When a direct prompt or CLI is sufficient
example: Format after edits with a hook; access an internal ticket system through MCP; keep API conventions in a skill.
mistakes: Turning every preference into a plugin
advancedVariation: Audit extension permissions and context cost periodically.

title: Increase autonomy with boundaries, not trust alone
summary: Allowlist narrow commands, use auto review where suitable, and isolate risky autonomous work.
explanation: Permission fatigue makes repeated clicking ineffective; scoped permissions and sandboxing preserve meaningful review.
whyItWorks: The blast radius is constrained even if the agent or input is wrong.
whenNotToUse: Unknown infrastructure or secrets without isolation
example: Allow npm test, keep push and deployment manual, and run experimental scripts in a disposable container.
advancedVariation: Use hooks to block sensitive paths and audit approved commands.

title: Debug from evidence, not confidence
summary: Reproduce, localize, form competing hypotheses, instrument, and falsify.
explanation: Requests for confidence or 'double-checking' are weaker than obtaining external evidence.
whyItWorks: Logs, tests, history, and minimal reproductions distinguish causes from plausible stories.
whenNotToUse: Do not add permanent instrumentation without review
example: Identify the first bad commit with git bisect driven by an automated reproduction.
advancedVariation: Ask a fresh session to falsify the leading hypothesis.

title: Review outputs at multiple levels
summary: Check requirement fit, architecture, diff, tests, runtime behavior, and residual risk.
explanation: Passing tests can coexist with scope creep, weak tests, security faults, or poor maintainability.
whyItWorks: Independent evidence covers different failure classes.
whenNotToUse: Never rely solely on self-review for high-risk changes
example: Have Claude summarize changed behavior and risks, then independently inspect the diff and execute checks.
mistakes: Letting the authoring context be the only reviewer
advancedVariation: Use a writer/reviewer session pair.

title: Automate only a proven loop
summary: First make the workflow observable and reliable; then encode it with narrow inputs and failure boundaries.
explanation: Non-interactive mode, hooks, and scripts amplify both correctness and mistakes.
whyItWorks: A mature loop has known preconditions, outputs, and recovery paths.
whenNotToUse: Ambiguous high-impact decisions
example: Run claude -p with structured output for a read-only CI report, validate the schema, and require human approval for edits.
advancedVariation: Fan out read-only analysis and aggregate results through a deterministic validator.

title: Use visual references and browser evidence for UI work
summary: A screenshot communicates layout intent; browser inspection verifies actual behavior.
explanation: Text specifications often omit spatial relationships and responsive behavior.
whyItWorks: Visual references constrain design while screenshots, DOM state, and console logs expose regressions.
whenNotToUse: Do not substitute screenshots for accessible text extraction or semantic tests
example: Supply a reference image, implement semantically, then verify at desktop and mobile sizes.
advancedVariation: Prefer DOM/accessibility-tree interactions for functional tests and screenshots for visual review.

title: Design the harness, not just the prompt
summary: The harness is the surrounding system that supplies context, tools, state, evaluation, retries, permissions, and observability.
explanation: The harness is the surrounding system that supplies context, tools, state, evaluation, retries, permissions, and observability.
whyItWorks: A strong model inside a weak harness still loops, loses state, or takes unsafe actions.
whenToUse: Use when moving from a demo to repeated or production work.
whenNotToUse: Do not build a platform before a simple verified loop proves the need.
example: Model → context assembly → tool call → state update → evaluator → bounded retry.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Separate context, state, and memory
summary: Context is what the model sees now; state is where the workflow is; memory is what should survive into later runs.
explanation: Context is what the model sees now; state is where the workflow is; memory is what should survive into later runs.
whyItWorks: Separating them prevents a transcript from becoming an unreliable database.
whenToUse: Use for multi-step or resumed work.
whenNotToUse: A small single-turn task may need none of them.
example: Context: relevant files. State: task 3 of 7. Memory: confirmed repository convention.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Treat tools as typed, observable interfaces
summary: A good agent tool has a narrow action, explicit inputs, structured output, predictable errors, and the least authority required.
explanation: A good agent tool has a narrow action, explicit inputs, structured output, predictable errors, and the least authority required.
whyItWorks: Clear interfaces reduce hallucinated calls and make failures debuggable.
whenToUse: Use whenever Claude reaches an API, CLI, MCP, browser, or custom script.
whenNotToUse: Do not wrap a reliable CLI without a measurable benefit.
example: Prefer get_issue(id) over a generic shell string that can do anything.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Orchestrate dependencies; parallelize independence
summary: Orchestration chooses order, ownership, handoffs, and integration across workers. Multi-agent systems help only when jobs are genuinely separable.
explanation: Orchestration chooses order, ownership, handoffs, and integration across workers. Multi-agent systems help only when jobs are genuinely separable.
whyItWorks: Explicit dependencies prevent duplicated work and conflicting writes.
whenToUse: Use for independent research, review, or isolated branches.
whenNotToUse: Keep tightly coupled design decisions with one owner.
example: Researcher → planner → writer, while independent security and test reviews fan out.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Put human gates at consequential boundaries
summary: Guardrails constrain what can happen; permissions constrain authority; human-in-the-loop gates reserve irreversible judgment for a person.
explanation: Guardrails constrain what can happen; permissions constrain authority; human-in-the-loop gates reserve irreversible judgment for a person.
whyItWorks: Safety comes from bounded consequences, not model confidence.
whenToUse: Use for writes, money, secrets, deployment, deletion, or external communication.
whenNotToUse: Avoid approval prompts for harmless deterministic reads that create fatigue.
example: Read automatically; draft a change; require approval before push or deploy.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Evaluate outcomes and trace the path
summary: Evals measure whether tasks succeed; observability records prompts, tool calls, state transitions, cost, latency, and failures so you can explain why.
explanation: Evals measure whether tasks succeed; observability records prompts, tool calls, state transitions, cost, latency, and failures so you can explain why.
whyItWorks: Without both, failures look random and improvements are anecdotes.
whenToUse: Use for repeated automation and production agents.
whenNotToUse: A one-off local edit may only need tests and a diff.
example: Track task success, invalid tool calls, retries, human overrides, time, and cost.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Define stopping, retry, and escalation conditions
summary: Every loop needs success, failure, budget, timeout, and human-escalation exits. Reflection must compare evidence to a measurable rule.
explanation: Every loop needs success, failure, budget, timeout, and human-escalation exits. Reflection must compare evidence to a measurable rule.
whyItWorks: An agent that can continue but cannot decide when to stop is an incident generator.
whenToUse: Use for any repeated or unattended loop.
whenNotToUse: Do not loop ambiguous creative work without review checkpoints.
example: Stop on verified acceptance; fail after N attempts or budget; escalate on permission or uncertainty.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Use Ralph loops only for atomic, verifiable work
summary: A Ralph loop repeatedly selects an unfinished task, works, tests, records progress, and continues until a machine-checkable completion condition or hard stop.
explanation: A Ralph loop repeatedly selects an unfinished task, works, tests, records progress, and continues until a machine-checkable completion condition or hard stop.
whyItWorks: Fresh iterations plus file-based state can recover from failures without carrying a decaying transcript.
whenToUse: Use for long tasks decomposed into single-iteration stories with reliable tests.
whenNotToUse: Avoid vague goals, unsafe host access, subjective design, or tasks without budgets.
example: PRD → prd.json passes flags → one story → tests → progress.txt → next iteration.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Layer CLAUDE.md at the narrowest useful scope
summary: Global, repository, local, and nested instructions should contain only stable rules appropriate to their scope.
explanation: Global, repository, local, and nested instructions should contain only stable rules appropriate to their scope.
whyItWorks: Scoped progressive disclosure keeps core context small while making specialized guidance available where used.
whenToUse: Use for monorepos, team conventions, and repeated project commands.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it as a linter, task log, or dump of every file.
example: Root holds shared commands; frontend/backend child files hold subsystem exceptions; personal notes stay local.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Let hooks enforce deterministic policy
summary: CLAUDE.md explains a rule; a hook executes or blocks deterministic behavior at the correct lifecycle event.
explanation: CLAUDE.md explains a rule; a hook executes or blocks deterministic behavior at the correct lifecycle event.
whyItWorks: Machines are better than prose at formatting, secret-path blocking, and required checks.
whenToUse: Use for stable fast checks with predictable exit status.
whenNotToUse: Avoid slow, flaky, destructive, or opaque hook actions.
example: Post-edit format; pre-command reject sensitive paths; stop hook verify completion.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Build a provenance-linked knowledge graph
summary: A graph turns isolated documents into connected concepts; an Obsidian vault makes the map browsable by Claude Code and people.
explanation: A graph turns isolated documents into connected concepts; an Obsidian vault makes the map browsable by Claude Code and people.
whyItWorks: Edges expose relationships file-by-file search misses, while source backlinks constrain hallucinated synthesis.
whenToUse: Use for large related document collections and recurring research.
whenNotToUse: Avoid generating hundreds of bare notes without a retrieval or review workflow.
example: Ingest docs → extract ideas/edges → export isolated vault → enrich notes → link each node to source → merge reversibly.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Optimize daily interface and feedback ergonomics
summary: Status lines, slash commands, aliases, voice input, compact output, session search, background work, and browser tools reduce coordination friction.
explanation: Status lines, slash commands, aliases, voice input, compact output, session search, background work, and browser tools reduce coordination friction.
whyItWorks: Small reductions in repeated interaction cost compound across many sessions.
whenToUse: Adopt after observing a repeated bottleneck.
whenNotToUse: Do not install every customization or patch the CLI without accepting maintenance risk.
example: Show branch/context status, dictate rich briefs, background long commands, and search local history.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
Expanding authority before proving the loop
advancedVariation: Combine this concept with independent evaluation and a strict resource budget.

title: Use Claude Code as a universal tool orchestrator—with review
summary: Claude Code can research, write Markdown, inspect CI, drive CLIs, test browsers, create artifacts, and connect remote workflows.
explanation: Claude Code can research, write Markdown, inspect CI, drive CLIs, test browsers, create artifacts, and connect remote workflows.
whyItWorks: The terminal provides a common interface to durable files and established tools.
whenToUse: Use when the task has accessible evidence and a verifiable output.
whenNotToUse: Do not treat generated research, prose, or operational changes as self-verifying.
example: Draft in Markdown, preserve links, investigate CI from logs/history, verify visually, then create a draft PR.
mistakes: Using the concept without a success measure
